ActorPoolAllocator: Internal JSL/JSR allocator that pops the next free actor slot from the LIFO free list at ($4E). On success returns carry clear with Y = new actor WRAM base ($1000 + index×$30) and zeroes the free-list entry; on pool exhaustion returns carry set with Y = $1FC0. Increments activeActorCount on allocation. Called by SpawnSceneActors, AllocateActorBefore/After, and SpawnBefore/After COP handlers.
AdhocVramDma: COP #4F with staged operands on first use: reads source word, byte, dest word, and size word into adhocVramDma staging and sets extendedFlags bit 0, then yields RTL. Later calls while bit 0 is set poll completion against the staged size; clears bit 0 and RTI to resume when done.
AdvanceMapY: Internal JSR helper that advances the collision map index in $001C by one tile row ($10 bytes within a page). When the low byte overflows (the row nibble wrapped past 15) it adds mapRowStrideL0 to a page byte taken from the accumulator's hidden high half (the caller's last 16-bit A, inferred to be the page of the last tile written; not reloaded from $1C), moving to the first row of the next page row. This matches the intended result only while the rectangle's row does not cross a page edge horizontally; ClearCollisionRect and its Full variant use a 16-bit ADC of mapBoundsX instead, which does not have this dependency. Called by MarkCollisionRect between rectangle rows.
AdvanceSpriteAnim: COP #56 with no operands. Indexes the spriteset table by anim index ($28) and frame counter ($2A), stages sprite-tile DMA via animScratch, and RTL while DMA is pending ($00B2); clears $2A and RTI when the frame sequence ends (negative entry).
AndExtraFlags: COP #5C with one word operand. ANDs the actor's extendedFlags word ($7F002A) with the operand, so the operand is a mask of bits to KEEP (e.g. #$FFF7 clears bit 3).
AnimFrameLookup: Internal JSR helper that maps an animation step index in A to a frame duration. Doubles A to index movement_delta_table and loads the duration byte. Called by StageSprX, StageSprY, StageSprXY, and their loop variants to convert COP animation operands into frame counts stored in $2C/$2E.
AnimLoop: COP #8A with no operands. Repeats UpdateActorAnimation until a cycle completes, then decrements sprTimer and loops the animation until the timer reaches zero before clearing deltas and continuing.
AnimOnce: COP #89 with no operands. Calls UpdateActorAnimation each frame, yielding RTL while animation is in progress; on completion clears movement deltas $2C/$2E and RTI.
AnimOneFrame: COP #8B with no operands. Calls UpdateActorAnimation once and always RTI; clears $2C/$2E if the animation sequence finished that frame.
ApplyBgChange: COP #33 with no operands. Renders one frame (UpdateFrameRender + UpdateFrameDialogue), then loops AnimateEventBlock — each call swaps tiles and queues the on-screen ones for VRAM until the queue is full or all tiles are done — with an UpdateFrameDialogue frame between calls to flush the queue. Carry set from AnimateEventBlock = all tiles processed. Ends with one more frame.
ApplyMoveToChild: COP #B0 with two byte operands (X index, Y index). Stages movement indices and AnimFrameLookup durations on the tail child actor referenced by $0058.
BindSineHdma: COP #61 with two word operands: HDMA table address and channel configuration. Ping-pongs the table pointer by +$0200 based on $0036 bit 0, then registers the channel through SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect.
bitmasks_bit_position: Shared 8-byte lookup table mapping bit indices 0–7 to single-bit mask bytes: $01, $02, $04, $08, $10, $20, $40, $80. Used by all Set/Clear/Test flag routines for bit-level access to the eventFlags and wramFlags arrays.
BossClearApplyStatReward:
Iterates enemy_clear_reward_table entries in the boss's range [$04.lo .. $0E].
Each entry byte is a reward type: 1=MaxHP+1, 2=STR+1, 3=DEF+1, 0=skip.
Uses per-enemy flags ($0300 range) to avoid granting the same reward twice.
BranchIfActorAt: COP #29 with one byte (actor list index), two words (X, Y), and one &Code operand. Resolves the actor via ResolveActorIndex then performs the same exact pixel coordinate compare as BranchIfPlayerAt.
BranchIfActorNear: COP #20 with one byte (actor list index), one byte (radius), and one &Code operand. Resolves the actor via ResolveActorIndex (index×$30+$1000) and branches if both Manhattan |ΔX| and |ΔY| are within (radius×16+1) pixels; otherwise skips the branch address.
BranchIfBehindWall:
COP #5D wall-occlusion branch taking one &Code operand. Converts the actor pixel position to tile coordinates, samples the collision layer via CalcTileMapOffset, and decides whether the tile hides the actor. If the actor is behind a wall (high nibble set, or a low nibble other than 0 or $0E, or the position is out of the map), the script jumps to the branch target; if it is visible, the operand is skipped and the script continues. The branch is taken on occlusion, as the COP name says.

When bit 4 of byte $0F of the actor (the high byte of oamXorFlags $0E; that is OAM attribute priority bit 0, inferred) is set, the handler takes the "layer-aware" path, where both outcomes of the tile test lead to "visible", so only the out-of-map check can occlude. Used by Eyesore, the diamond-mine enemies, and similar actors.
BranchIfBodyNe: COP #49 with one byte (expected form ID) plus one &Code branch. Branches to the target offset when characterForm ($0AD4) does not match the operand; if the form matches, skips the branch.
BranchIfCollisionTypeNe: COP #62 with one byte (collision type nibble) and one &Code branch target. Samples the collision layer at the actor's tile via CalcTileMapOffset; jumps to the branch target when the tile's low nibble EQUALS the operand or the position is out of bounds, otherwise skips the branch operand. The COP name BranchIfCollisionTypeNe says "not equal" but the code branches on equality (BEQ). The solid nibble is ignored: a solid tile whose low nibble matches also branches. The operand is stored in absolute $0000 (global scratch) before D is zeroed, then compared with CMP $00, which reads the same location.
BranchIfDirToPlayer: COP #2F with one byte (direction) and one &Code operand. Branches if ComputeDirectionToPlayer from the actor matches the operand direction; otherwise skips the branch address.
BranchIfDirToPlayerFrom: COP #30 with two signed byte offsets (X, Y), one byte (direction), and one &Code operand. Same as BranchIfDirToPlayer but computes direction from an offset reference point added to the actor position.
BranchIfHasItem: COP #D6 with one byte (item ID) and one &Code operand. Calls CheckInventoryForItem; branches to the &Code offset when the item is present (carry clear = found).
BranchIfItemEquipped: COP #D7 with one byte (item ID) and one &Code operand. Compares the operand against inventorySlots[inventoryEquippedIndex]; branches to &Code when they match. inventorySlots is a 16-byte array ($0AB4–$0AC3, one item ID per byte; CheckInventoryForItem steps it with INY), so the index is a plain byte index. When nothing is equipped (index $FFFF, e.g. after RemoveItem) the indexed read wraps to $0AB3 — the byte before the array — so the compare reads unrelated data (analysis only, unverified at runtime).
BranchIfNotOnGridline: COP #1F with one &Code operand. Branches when the actor is off the 16-pixel grid: either its Y has a non-zero low nibble, or its X plus the metasprite hitbox X offset (hitbox byte 0, forced negative by ORA #$FF00) has one. Falls through (operand skipped) only when both are aligned. DBR is switched to the sprite-data bank ($7F0008,X) to read the hitbox header and restored on both exits.
BranchIfNotPressed: COP #41 with one word (button mask, bit 0 selects joypadRaw) plus one &Code branch target. Jumps to the target when none of the masked buttons is down in the selected source, otherwise skips the target operand. Inverse of BranchIfPressed.
BranchIfOffCamera: COP #68 with one &Code operand. Compares the actor position ($14 = X, $16 = Y) against the camera window: cameraOffsetX/Y (left/top limit) and cameraBoundsX/Y (right/bottom limit), the active map window's scroll limits per docs/wram-memory-map.md. If both axes are inside the window the operand is skipped and the script continues; otherwise the script jumps to the operand. A negative position counts as outside, the lower limit is inclusive and the upper limit exclusive (position ≥ limit = outside). Used by enemy scripts (e.g. awB0_zip_fly, pyD2_haunt, gw83_asp, gw82_fire_bug, av6D_dive_bat).
BranchIfPlayerAt: COP #28 with two words (X, Y) and one &Code operand. Branches if the player's exact pixel coordinates match the operand position; otherwise skips the branch address.
BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles: COP #45 with four byte operands (min tile X, max tile X, min tile Y, max tile Y) plus one &Code branch. Converts tile coords to pixels (×16) and branches if the player actor's position falls inside the rectangle (Y compared against player Y minus 8).
BranchIfPlayerInRelTiles: COP #44 relative tile-region branch taking four signed byte offsets (minX, maxX, minY, maxY) plus one &Code operand. Builds a pixel rectangle relative to the current actor position and tests whether the player actor falls inside it on both axes. If the player is inside, the script jumps to the branch target; otherwise it skips the six-byte operand block.
BranchIfPlayerNear: COP #21 with one byte (radius) and one &Code operand. Shares the same Manhattan proximity test as BranchIfActorNear but compares against playerActor instead of a script-specified actor index.
BranchIfPressed: COP #40 with one word (button mask, bit 0 selects joypadRaw) plus one &Code branch target (same bank as the script). Jumps to the target if any masked button is down, otherwise skips the two-byte target. Never yields; used heavily by the player actor (walk, ladder and shimmy state machines).
BranchIfSolidEast: COP #18 with one &Code operand. Queries the tile one column east (X + $10) and branches on the same solid-nibble test pattern.
BranchIfSolidHere: COP #13 with one &Code operand. Probes the actor's own tile with TileCollisionQuery and branches to the target when the result has any bit of $000F set: the tile is blocked (high nibble set), the probe is outside the camera bounds, or the tile's terrain type is non-zero. Otherwise the operand is skipped. The same $000F test is used by the directional variants (#15–#18).
BranchIfSolidNorth: COP #15 with one &Code operand. Queries the tile one row north (Y − $10) via TileCollisionQuery and branches to the script offset when the result has any lower-nibble bit set.
BranchIfSolidOffset: COP #14 with two signed byte tile offsets plus one &Code operand. Sign-extends and ×16-scales each offset, adds them to the actor position, runs TileCollisionQuery at the resulting pixel position, and branches on the same $000F test as BranchIfSolidHere. It repeats the offset math of ParseSignedTileOffset inline but keeps pixel units (TileCollisionQuery does the tile conversion and its own −1 row adjustment).
BranchIfSolidSouth: COP #16 with one &Code operand. Queries the tile one row south (Y + $10) and branches on the same lower-nibble solid test as BranchIfSolidHere.
BranchIfSolidWest: COP #17 with one &Code operand. Queries the tile one column west (X − $10) and branches if TileCollisionQuery reports a set lower-nibble bit.
BranchIfTypeEast: COP #1E with one byte type and one &Code operand. Compares collision type at X + $10 and branches to &Code on match.
BranchIfTypeHere: COP #1A (copdef name BranchIfSolidType) with one byte (expected type) plus one &Code operand. TileCollisionQuery at the actor position; branches if the low byte of the result equals the operand. Blocked and out-of-bounds probes return $0F, so they match an operand of $0F. On a mismatch the pushed result is popped into Y (Y is clobbered; X and D still hold the slot).
BranchIfTypeNorth: COP #1B with one byte type and one &Code operand. Compares the collision type at Y − $10 against the operand and branches on equality.
BranchIfTypeSouth: COP #1C with one byte type and one &Code operand. Same type comparison as BranchIfTypeHere but samples the tile at Y + $10.
BranchIfTypeWest: COP #1D with one byte type and one &Code operand. Compares collision type at X − $10 and branches to &Code on match.
BranchNearerAxis: COP #2C with two &Code operands. Compares absolute |ΔX| vs |ΔY| to the player; branches to operand[0] if Y is the nearer axis, operand[1] if X is nearer or equal.
BranchOnFlagByte: COP #D0 with one byte (flag), one byte (sense), and one &Code operand. Tests the flag via TestEventFlag; the sense byte selects branch-on-set vs branch-on-clear, jumping to the &Code offset when the condition matches.
BranchOnFlagWord: COP #D1 with one word (flag), one byte (sense), and one &Code operand. Word-indexed variant of BranchOnFlagByte with the same sense-controlled conditional branch.
BranchOnPlayerFacing: COP #31 with four &Code operands. Calls GetPlayerFacingDirection and dispatches to one of four branch targets for player facing values 0–3.
BranchOnPlayerX: COP #2A with one word (threshold) and three &Code addresses (west, center, east). Three-way branch on horizontal player offset: zero delta → center, |ΔX| within threshold → center, beyond threshold → west or east.
BranchOnPlayerY: COP #2B with one word (threshold) and three &Code addresses (above, center, below). Same three-way logic as BranchOnPlayerX but compares vertical player offset on Y.
BuildSineHdmaTable:
Internal JSR helper that fills two interleaved HDMA indirect-data tables with per-scanline scroll offsets derived from sine_table_8bit.

Computes a double-buffered WRAM table base from spritesetPtr + $0100, ping-ponging by $0200 on $0036 bit 0 (frame parity). Divides $0100 by half the scanline count to compute a per-scanline sine table step size, then iterates through all scanlines: looks up sine_table_8bit at the current angle, multiplies by actor amplitude ($7F0008) via SNES hardware multiply, handles sign correction for negative sine values, and writes camera-offset scroll values into both horizontal ($62) and vertical ($5E) HDMA data regions.

Called by TickSineHdma with camera coordinates in DP $18 (X) and $1C (Y). Operates in data bank $7E with DP zeroed. Returns via RTS.
BuildSineLookupTable:
Internal helper that fills the 512-byte sineTableA ($7E8900) and sineTableB ($7E8B00) arrays with amplitude-scaled sine values.

Guard conditions: proceeds only if displayModeFlags bit 6 ($0040) is set or animScratch2 bit 0 ($0001) is set; clears the trigger bit after acknowledging it. This ensures tables are only regenerated when flagged as needed by the HDMA system.

Reads actor amplitude from $7F0008 into WRMPYA, then iterates 256 word entries: looks up each sine sample from sine_table_8bit at step intervals of $0E, multiplies by amplitude via hardware multiply, corrects negative samples (multiply RDMPYH by $FF, add RDMPYL for sign extension), and writes the scaled 16-bit result to both sineTableA and sineTableB at the same index.

Called by GenHdmaSine (COP #00) to populate the full sine tables used by HDMA wave effects. Returns via RTS.
CallNear: COP #C8 with one &Code operand. Saves the current return PC in retPtr1, then RTI-jumps to the same-bank &Code target.
CallNearDeferred: COP #C9 with one &Code operand. Sets $00 to the target &Code offset, saves the return PC in retPtr1, and yields via RTL so the callee runs next frame.
CameraPanDown: COP #DC (script name PanCameraDown) southward camera pan with no operands. Decrements the per-actor frame counter at $2A each invocation; when it underflows, reloads from CameraScrollStepLookup using the speed index in $2B low nibble, then adds that step to cameraTargetY. Yields via RTL until cameraTargetY reaches cameraBoundsY, then resumes the script. Called from forced_walk and other cutscene scroll actors.
CameraPanLeft: COP #DF with no operands. Decrements $2A, fetches scroll step from CameraScrollStepLookup, subtracts from cameraTargetX, and yields RTL until cameraTargetX reaches cameraOffsetX.
CameraPanRight: COP #DE with no operands. Decrements $2A, fetches scroll step from CameraScrollStepLookup, adds to cameraTargetX, and yields RTL until cameraTargetX reaches cameraBoundsX.
CameraPanUp: COP #DD with no operands. Mirrors CameraPanDown: decrements $2A, reloads scroll step from CameraScrollStepLookup via $2B low nibble, subtracts from cameraTargetY, and yields RTL until cameraTargetY reaches cameraOffsetY.
CameraScrollStepLookup: Reads the next scroll speed entry from the table at scrollStepTableBase, indexed by scrollStepIndex. Increments the index and doubles it for word access. Returns carry clear with the speed value in A when the entry high byte is non-zero (valid step); returns carry set and resets scrollStepIndex to zero when a zero high-byte terminator is reached. Called by all four CameraPan handlers (Down/Up/Right/Left) to fetch per-frame scroll step values.
CardinalToPlayer: COP #35 with no operands. Returns 0–3 (N/E/S/W) by comparing absolute X and Y deltas to the player and selecting the cardinal axis with the larger magnitude.
ClearAllWramFlags: JSL helper that zero-fills the entire $20-byte wramFlags region at $0A80. Uses a word-wide STA loop (16 iterations × 2 bytes = 32 bytes). Called on scene transitions to reset all temporary WRAM flags.
ClearCollisionHere: COP #11 with no operands. Calls ClearCollisionRect with flag $0001, which routes to ClearCollisionRectFull and ANDs #$00 on every hitbox tile to zero both solid and type nibbles.
ClearCollisionRect: Internal JSR helper that clears solid flags from a rectangle on the collision map. Reads the metasprite hitbox exactly like MarkCollisionRect, then ANDs #$0F on every tile in the rectangle to remove the solid nibble while preserving the type nibble. If the flag word in WRAM $0000 is nonzero it jumps to ClearCollisionRectFull instead. Row stepping is inlined: +$10 on the low byte, and on carry the page byte is advanced by adding the word mapBoundsX (see the note at that ADC). Called by ClearSolidHere (flag 0) and ClearCollisionHere (flag 1).
ClearCollisionRectFull: Internal subroutine reached via JMP from ClearCollisionRect when the full-clear flag ($0001) is set. ANDs #$00 on every tile in the metasprite hitbox rectangle, zeroing both the solid and type nibbles. Used by ClearCollisionHere to completely remove collision data at the actor footprint.
ClearEventFlag: Core JSR routine that clears one bit in the eventFlags ($0A00) bitfield. Loads the bitmasks_bit_position entry, inverts it via EOR #$FF to create a clear mask, then ANDs against the eventFlags byte. Called by ClearFlag COP handlers and JSL wrappers.
ClearFlag_0100: JSL helper that clears an event flag at base $0100. Masks to byte, adds $0100, and calls ClearEventFlag.
ClearFlagByte: COP #CE with one byte operand. Calls ClearEventFlag on the byte flag index.
ClearFlagRaw: JSL helper that clears an event flag without adding a base offset. Masks to byte and calls ClearEventFlag directly.
ClearFlagWord: COP #CF with one word operand. Calls ClearEventFlag on the word flag index.
ClearHMirror: COP #BA with no operands. Clears horizontal mirror bit $4000 on OAM attribute word $0E via TRB.
ClearPriorityMax: COP #B4 with no operands. Clears bit $0002 on actor+$10 via TRB, removing the front-most override (Y-based sorting resumes unless bit $0001 is set).
ClearPriorityMin: COP #B5 with no operands. Clears bit $0001 on actor+$10 via TRB, removing the rear-most override (Y-based sorting resumes unless bit $0002 is set).
ClearSolidAbs: COP #10 with two byte operands (absolute tile X and Y). Resolves the map index and ANDs #$0F on that collisionLayer byte to remove solid flags.
ClearSolidHere: COP #0C with no operands. Copies the actor pixel position into the probe scratch $18/$1C and calls ClearCollisionRect with flag $0000, ANDing #$0F on every collisionLayer tile in the metasprite hitbox to clear the solid nibble while preserving the terrain type nibble.
ClearSolidOffset: COP #0E with two signed byte tile offsets. Uses the same ParseSignedTileOffset path as MarkSolidOffset, then ANDs #$0F on one collisionLayer tile to clear the solid nibble only.
ClearTypeAbs: COP #12 with two byte operands (absolute tile X and Y). Converts to a map index and ANDs #$F0 on the collision byte, clearing only the type nibble while leaving solid flags intact.
ComputeDirectionToPlayer: Internal JSR helper that computes an 8-direction octant index (0–7) from the reference point in $0018/$001C (pixels) to the player position. Compass order is clockwise from north: 0=N, 1=NE, 2=E, 3=SE, 4=S, 5=SW, 6=W, 7=NW (not the same numbering as GetPlayerFacingDirection). Rule: if |ΔY| < $10 the result is pure E or W whatever ΔX is (including the player standing on the reference point, which gives E); otherwise the vertical component is N or S, and it becomes a diagonal only when |ΔX| ≥ $10. Returns the octant in A. Called by DirToPlayer, DirToPlayerFrom, BranchIfDirToPlayer and BranchIfDirToPlayerFrom (cop_handlers_player_query).
ComputeFollowAngle:
Computes the angular step for smooth follow when horizontal separation dominates.

Inputs are absolute delta-X ($0018) and delta-Y ($001C) prepared by InitFollowAndChase; if equal, stores angle zero. Otherwise divides the smaller axis by 16 and calls hardware_math.UnsignedDivide to map the ratio into a 0–23 orbit index. Stores the result in orbitAngle ($7F0010,X), clears orbitDiameter, and returns via RTS.
ComputeScrollDeltas:
Computes scroll velocity for both axes using the hardware multiply/divide unit.

For each axis: loads the speed parameter ($14 for X, $16 for Y) and camera target position (cameraTargetX $06BE or cameraTargetY $06C2), then calls hardware_math.MulDivide via JSL. The result is stored to cameraDeltaX ($06C0) or cameraDeltaY ($06C4).

If a speed parameter is zero, the corresponding MulDivide call and delta store are skipped entirely (the axis remains at its previous value). This allows selective axis computation — e.g., ScrollCameraVertical only sets $16 nonzero.
cop_dispatch_table: 227-entry handler pointer table mapping COP opcodes $00–$6D and $80–$E2 (209 valid) to short-address handler labels across 13 handler blocks. Opcodes $6E–$7F are an 18-entry #$0000 gap that would crash if executed.
cop_table_sentinel: End-of-table guard: a NOP/BRA infinite loop that catches any opcode past $E2, preventing execution from falling into unmapped ROM.
CopDispatch: Central COP bytecode dispatcher reached from CopVector. Reads the opcode byte from the script stream at [$0A], doubles it as a word index, and indirect-jumps through cop_dispatch_table to the matching handler. Sets up X=Y=ActorID, script pointer $0A, and bank byte $0C from the COP interrupt stack frame.
CopVector: COP software interrupt vector. Jumps to the COP dispatch handler which implements the game's scripting command system.
CopyPalette: COP #50 with five operands: word source base, byte bank, byte source palette index, byte dest palette index, byte count. Copies palette entries through the $0402 DMA helper into CGRAM staging (indices scaled ×2, dest base $0A00).
CopyPosToNext: COP #47 with no operands. Copies the current actor's pixel position ($14/$16) to the next linked actor at offset $06.
CopyPosToPrev: COP #46 with no operands. Copies the current actor's pixel position ($14/$16) to the previous linked actor at offset $04.
CopySiblingFollowState:
Lightweight entry into the smooth-follow engine that mirrors state from a sibling actor.

Reads the sibling actor ID at $0004,Y, swaps loopCounter ($7F0014) and chatPtr ($7F000A) between sibling and self, then branches into the shared chase loop without resetting direction state in animScratch2. Spawned via SpawnMarkedAfter from boss and puzzle scripts.
Decompress: COP #51 with word source pointer, byte source bank, and word VRAM destination. Calls QuintetLzDecompress then ClearActorRenderList before resuming the script.
DialogueOptions: COP #BE with one word (option layout pointer) plus one word (branch table base). Requires worldReadyFlag == $000F; sets dialogue mode ($2000), masks inventory input ($0F00), calls MenuSelectionHandler, and branches into the table entry for the chosen option.
Die: COP #E0 with no operands. If actor flag bit $0040 on $12 is set, routes through DieNow_UnlinkChildren to cascade-remove linked child actors by parentId match; otherwise calls UnlinkActor directly. Returns via RTL to terminate the script.
DieNow_UnlinkChildren:
Cascade child-actor removal for Die/MarkDeath when actor flag $0040 is set.

The entry point (PLA/TAX/TCD/PLA/PLA/RTL) is the normal non-child Die exit. The shared child-removal code at loc_00A60E walks the doubly-linked actor list both backward ($04 pointers) and forward ($06 pointers) from the dying actor, collecting contiguous runs of actors whose parentId matches the dying actor. It then returns all collected child slots via ReturnActorSlot and patches the list pointers with three cases: head-removed (new head = forward boundary), tail-removed (new tail = backward boundary), or mid-list splice (link boundaries to each other).
DirToPlayer: COP #2D with no operands. Sets reference coordinates from the actor's $14/$16 and returns a 0–7 octant direction in A via ComputeDirectionToPlayer.
DirToPlayerFrom: COP #2E with two signed byte operands (X, Y pixel offsets). Adds sign-extended offsets to the actor position as the reference point and returns 0–7 direction via ComputeDirectionToPlayer.
DrawMetatileAbs: COP #4B metatile painter taking three byte operands: absolute tile X, tile Y, and metatile ID. Passes through TileQueryGate (RTL early-out if a tile query is already pending), converts tile coords to pixel positions, and calls ResolveTileData to update mapLayerTilemap and collisionLayer and queue BG VRAM tile writes when the target lies on screen. Used heavily in puzzle rooms and mine collapse scenes to swap floor/wall tiles.
DrawMetatileHere: COP #4C with one byte operand (metatile ID). Uses the actor's pixel position ($14/$16), passes TileQueryGate, then calls ResolveTileData to write mapLayerTilemap/collisionLayer and queue on-screen BG VRAM tile updates.
effect_position_update:
Integrating scroll actor that advances forced camera motion with hard bounds.

Each tick converts actor coordinates to velocity ($2C/$2E), adds effectDeltaX/Y, clamps cameraDeltaX against effectBoundsX and cameraDeltaY against effectBoundsY, then writes render deltas to $06E8/$06EA. Pairs with effect_velocity_init and effect_subpixel_math in the visual_effect_pipeline block.
effect_subpixel_math:
Per-frame subpixel scroll refinement actor spawned alongside effect_position_update.

On entry calls SetEntryHere and accumulates fractional scroll: when $14 has a nonzero high byte it scales through hardware_math.MulDivide against cameraTargetX into forcedScrollOverride; otherwise sign-extends and adds the low byte directly. Used in Sky Garden viper lair and mystic-statue sequences for smooth cinematic pans.
effect_velocity_init:
Visual-effect actor that seeds forced camera scroll from actor placement coordinates.

Converts actor $14/$16 (pixel position) into signed scroll velocities at $2C/$2E, zeroes integrated position state, waits one frame, then adds effectDeltaX/Y from the camera_scroll_controller and writes forcedScrollOverride ($06C8) with bit 15 set. Spawned in Babel Tower plane-jump and other cutscene scenes.
EnemyGemDropRouter:
Gem-type dispatcher called from StandardEnemyDefeatHandler when the enemy's stats byte at offset $03 is nonzero and scene flag $0300 is clear.

Uses the kill-count value in orbitAngle: two DEC operations select among three DarkGemDropSystem spawn targets (type 1, type 2, or weighted random). Each path spawns a gem actor via SpawnLastRel then jumps back for the remainder of the defeat sequence.
ExecuteVramDma:
Executes a single VRAM DMA transfer using pre-staged parameters.

Reads transfer parameters from direct page:
- $00B2: byte count (0 = skip)
- $00B0: VRAM destination address
- $00AC-$00AE: ROM/RAM source address (16-bit + bank)

Triggers DMA channel 0 and clears the byte count to prevent re-triggering.
FadeThenStartMusic: COP #05 with one byte operand (music bundle ID). Allocates a thinker actor after the current one via AllocateActorAfter, sets entry to SpcCheckMusicReady (fade-before-play path), sets thinker flag #$1000, clears render flag #$0800, and stores the music ID in chatPtr.
field_reveal_flash: Flash effect: plays reveal SFX and animates one flash sprite frame, then dies.
field_reveal_scatter:
Scatter particle: randomizes position using range from parent ($20=X range, $22=Y range).
Range tiers: 0-1 = ±$0F, 2-3 = ±$1F, 4+ = ±$3F pixels. LSR+carry sets sign (50/50 ±).
FillWramBlock:
Fills the OAM staging buffer at WRAM $0422 with the byte value $E0 via DMA.

Uses DMA fixed-source mode ($08) to repeat a single byte across 512 bytes of the OAM buffer. The fill value $E0 sets all sprite Y positions to 224 (off the bottom of the visible 224-line display), effectively hiding all OAM entries before sprite composition begins each frame.

Target: WRAM data port ($2180), size: $0200 (512 bytes = 128 OAM entries × 4 bytes).
ForceDirBoth: COP #AF with one byte operand (nonzero sets, zero clears). TSB or TRB bits $6000 on actor flags $12 to force or release both diagonal direction bits.
ForceDirNE: COP #AE with one byte operand (nonzero sets, zero clears). TSB or TRB bit $2000 on actor flags $12 to force or release northeast-facing direction.
ForceDirSW: COP #AD with one byte operand (nonzero sets, zero clears). TSB or TRB bit $4000 on actor flags $12 to force or release southwest-facing direction.
ForcedWalkSouth:
Cutscene auto-walk actor spawned on the player by StartForcedWalk during extended warp transitions.

Masks all joypad input, indexes forced_walk_sequence_table from scrollStepTableBase, stages south-facing player sprites via ReadDirSprite_YVelocity, pans the camera down (PanCameraDown), applies scroll offsets, re-syncs the player sprite, and calls SyncPlayerToCamera before dying. Default direction when no east/west/north bit is set.
GenHdmaSine: COP #00 sine-wave HDMA table generator with no operands (2 sites: sine_hdma_ending_wave and the unused gen_hdma_sine_oneshot). First calls BuildSineLookupTable, which refills the two 256-word tables sineTableA ($7E8900) and sineTableB ($7E8B00, a copy directly after A) from the actor amplitude $7F0008, but only when displayModeFlags bit 6 or animScratch2 bit 0 requests it. Then it writes a 7-byte indirect HDMA table at $7E8800: [$FF, pointer, $E0, pointer+$FE, $00], i.e. 127 repeat-mode scanlines followed by 96 (223 in total), each scanline taking one word from a window of the sine data. spritesetPtr is a phase counter incremented on every call; the window starts at sineTableA + (counter AND $01FE), so the wave slides by one word every second call. It is not a double buffer. A following COP QueueHdma ($7E8800 with B-bus #0F or #10, i.e. BG2HOFS/BG2VOFS) binds the table to a channel.
GetPlayerFacing: COP #48 with no operands. Saves the script return address and calls GetPlayerFacingDirection; the facing value (0–3) is returned in accumulator A on RTI.
GiveItem: COP #D4 with one byte (item ID) and one &Code (overflow handler). Calls GiveItemToPlayer; on success (carry clear) skips the overflow branch, on failure (carry set, inventory full) jumps to the &Code overflow target. Side effects of GiveItemToPlayer: the item ID is stored at $0DB8 for the dialogue text, and Y returns a dialogue string pointer that this handler ignores (scripts show their own dialogue).
HaltIfMaxFrames: COP #69 with one word operand (frame threshold). Compares it with the global timeline counter $00E4 (mnemonic actorLimitThreshold; the ending-credits actors keep it running, e.g. code_09E919 in sF7_credits increments it each tick, and it is $FFFF while stopped). While the counter is NOT above the threshold (counter ≤ threshold, unsigned) the handler rewinds the actor's entry pointer ($00) to this COP, discards the COP frame and yields with RTL, so the COP runs again next tick. Once the counter is above the threshold the script continues via RTI. Used as a timeline wait in the ending credits.
HalveMovementDistance:
Iterative distance halver called by StageMove when the pixel distance high byte is non-zero.

Halves both moveXAlt and moveYAlt via LSR, then increments a halving-pass counter in chatPtr. StageMove calls this in a loop until the distance fits in a single byte, enabling the hardware divider to compute per-frame velocity accurately.
IncanRuinsTransformPaletteFinal: Final phase: kill sibling thinkers, fill CGRAM with transformed palette, loop #36
IncanRuinsTransformPaletteWarmup: Warmup phase: alternate between palette #34 and #33 until flag $FF clears
InitGravity: COP #63 with one signed byte (initial velocity), one byte (acceleration factor), and one signed byte (target Y tile offset). Seeds scratch1010 gravity state and computes the absolute target Y in moveYAlt from the actor's current $16 position.
InitSineHdma: COP #5F with one word (WRAM base for four interleaved HDMA tables) and one byte (scanline count). Builds four staggered HDMA channel tables, scales amplitude via UnsignedDivide, and initializes sine-HDMA state in animScratch/retPtr1.
InitSmoothMovement:
Computes interpolation setup for MoveToward on first entry.

Converts moveXAlt/moveYAlt from absolute target coordinates to signed deltas from the current position ($14/$16), takes their absolute values, caps each at $00FE when the high byte is non-zero, and records the sign of each axis in $0004 via ROR. Selects the larger axis as the travel distance, divides by the frame-count operand via UnsignedDivide for per-frame velocity, zeroes animScratch/tick state, and sets extendedFlags bit 1 to mark smooth movement active.
InitSpiral: COP #6C spiral-orbit initializer taking two byte operands: starting orbitDiameter and orbitAngle. Stores both values into the corresponding actor WRAM fields ($7F0010/$7F0012) for use by the paired SpiralStep COP handler. Does not move the actor itself; it only seeds orbital motion state. Used by Mu vampires bat-spawn patterns.
IrqHandler: IRQ handler stub. Returns immediately via RTI since no hardware IRQ sources are enabled.
IrqVector: Hardware IRQ vector. Jumps to IrqHandler (currently a stub — hardware IRQs are unused).
JumpAfterDelay: COP #C3 with one Address (target) plus one word (frame delay). Sets actor $00/$02 to the target script pointer, stores the delay word in $08, and yields via RTL.
JumpFar: COP #C7 with one Address operand (word+bank). Cross-bank jump: writes the far entry to $00/$02 and updates the bank byte on the stack; RTI-resumes immediately at the target.
JumpNextFrame: COP #C4 with one Address operand. Sets $00/$02 to the target entry, zeroes the frame timer ($08), and yields via RTL for a one-frame deferred jump.
KillNext: COP #A9 with no operands. Switches context to the next linked actor ($06) and unlinks it via UnlinkActor.
KillPrev: COP #A8 with no operands. Switches context to the previous linked actor ($04) and unlinks it via UnlinkActor.
KillThinker: COP #3D with no operands. Unlinks the calling thinker from the doubly-linked thinker list ($005A head / $005C tail), then returns its slot to the thinker free list (long pointer $52/$54): the pointer is backed up one word and the slot address stored there, the reverse of ThinkerPoolAlloc. When the removed thinker was the only one, $5C is not reset (it still names the freed slot).
loc_00EB85: Compute scroll deltas for the visual effect pipeline
LockPlayerForClimb:
Shared helper that freezes the player for a stair-climb animation sequence.

Takes the climb frame count from actor parameter $0E (shifted left twice into statsPtr at $7F0020), zeros player velocity words at $002C/$002E/$0008, masks directional joypad input ($0F00 in joypadMaskStd), and sets playerFlags bit $0800. Called by all four StairTrigger handlers immediately before the player script switches to a Climb* routine.
LoopEnd: COP #CB with no operands. Decrements the active loop counter (player or actor variant); if non-zero, restores the saved loop-head PC and yields RTL, otherwise falls through and RTI-continues past the loop.
LoopStart: COP #CA with one byte operand (iteration count). For the player actor (X≥$1000) stores the count in loopCounter ($7F0014) and saves the loop-head PC in retPtr2; for scene actors uses loopCounterActor ($7F2102) and loopStartPcActor ($7F2100).
MarkCollisionRect: Internal JSR helper that marks a solid rectangle on the collision map. The actor's metasprite hitbox header (4 bytes at metaspritePtr, read in the sprite-data bank: X offset, Y offset, width in tiles, height in tiles) is combined with the pixel position in $0018/$001C (X/Y offsets are forced negative with ORA #$FF00), converted to a starting tile, and $F0 is ORed onto every collisionLayer byte of the rectangle. Columns step +1, crossing to the next 16-tile page with +$F0; rows step with AdvanceMapY. The whole rectangle is skipped if the starting index is ≥ $4000. Called only by MarkSolidHere (the other mark ops write a single tile).
MarkDeath: COP #A7 with no operands. Unlinks the actor via UnlinkActor; if actor flag bit $0040 on $12 is set, first cascade-unlinks child actors sharing the same parentId, then resumes the calling script via MarkDeathResumeHandler.
MarkDeathResumeHandler:
PEA/RTS return target reached from MarkDeath when the dying actor has child flag $0040 set.

Restores the actor's direct page (TCD) and index register (TAX) from the stack after the child-unlinking code in loc_00A60E completes, then RTIs to resume the calling script. Separated from MarkDeath because the child-unlinking path is shared with Die via BRA loc_00A60E.
MarkSolidAbs: COP #0F with two byte operands (absolute tile X and Y). Converts coordinates through TileCoordsToMapIndex and ORs #$F0 onto the collision byte at that index.
MarkSolidHere: COP #0B (legacy name SolidHighHere) collision marker with no operands. Copies the actor pixel position from $14/$16 into the probe scratch $18/$1C and calls MarkCollisionRect to OR $F0 onto every collision-layer tile covered by the actor's metasprite hitbox (the terrain nibble is preserved). The STZ $0000 beforehand is only meaningful to the Clear variants; MarkCollisionRect ignores it. Used by nearly every solid NPC, enemy and prop (462 call sites).
MarkSolidOffset: COP #0D with two signed byte operands (tile X/Y offsets). ParseSignedTileOffset sign-extends each offset, scales by 16 pixels, converts to tile coordinates (Y adjusted −16), then ORs #$F0 onto the single collisionLayer byte at that map index.
MovementVelocityCompute:
Per-axis velocity calculator for TickMove.

Writes the axis distance byte to WRMPYB, reads the multiply product from RDMPYL into WRDIVL, divides by animScratch2−1 (frame count) via WRDIVB, waits 5 NOPs for divider latency, then returns the per-frame pixel step in A ($0000). Called twice per TickMove tick: once for Y axis, once for X axis.
MoveToward: COP #22 with two byte operands (animation index, frame count). On first entry InitSmoothMovement computes per-frame velocity from moveXAlt/moveYAlt deltas via UnsignedDivide and sets extendedFlags bit 1; subsequent calls interpolate position each frame using hardware multiply/divide and yield RTL until the frame count expires.
MoveTowardFinish:
Cleanup exit for MoveToward when the frame counter matches the target tick count.

Clears extendedFlags bit 1 (smooth move active) via AND #$FFFD, skips the two-byte operand by advancing $0A, and yields RTL to resume the calling script. Called via JMP from MoveToward when animScratch2 low byte equals $24.
MultiplyThenDivide:
Chained hardware multiply→divide for per-frame interpolation velocity.

Writes the axis distance byte to WRMPYB (starting the multiply), reads the product from RDMPYL into WRDIVL as the dividend, uses animScratch2−1 as the frame-count divisor in WRDIVB, and returns the quotient (pixels per frame) in A via $0000. When the divisor is zero (BEQ), skips the divide to avoid a division-by-zero hang. Called twice per MoveToward tick for X and Y axes.
MusicAndText: COP #19 with one byte (track ID), one word (text pointer), and one byte (data bank). On pool success, allocates via ActorPoolAllocator, copies actor state, sets MusicPlaybackActor, and stores operands in $0026/$0020/$0022. On pool exhaustion, falls back to inline DialogStringRenderer with temporary data bank, joypad input suppressed, and displayModeFlags bit $80 cleared.
NmiHandler:
V-Blank interrupt handler — the critical per-frame DMA orchestration routine.

Execution order during V-Blank:
1. Save registers and set data bank to $81
2. Disable HDMA to prevent bus conflicts
3. Upload scroll registers to PPU
4. DMA tilemap strip updates (dirty column/row data)
5. DMA CGRAM palette (512 bytes from $7F0A00)
6. DMA OAM table (544 bytes from $0422)
7. DMA sprite VRAM tiles
8. Configure VRAM DMA mode ($80 word-access, $18 target, $01 two-reg)
9. Conditional: full tilemap DMA or skip based on displayModeFlags bit 3
10. Execute queued VRAM writes and pending DMA
11. Re-enable HDMA channels
12. Poll joypad (spin-wait for auto-read completion)
13. Handle music transition state (run full frame update if fading)
14. Send audio commands to SPC on alternate frames
15. Increment frame parity counter and restore registers
NmiVector: NMI (V-Blank) interrupt vector. Jumps to the NMI handler for per-frame DMA transfers and display updates.
NudgePosition: COP #BC with two signed byte operands (delta X, delta Y). Sign-extends each byte and adds the offsets to the actor's pixel position at $14/$16.
OrExtraFlags: COP #5B with one word operand. ORs the value into the actor's extendedFlags word at $7F002A.
PaletteRestart: COP #36 with no operands. Restarts the bundle whose ID is already in animScratch+2: branches into the shared tail of PaletteStart (loc_009370), which zeroes the sub-entry index, loads and applies sub-entry 0, saves the resume address and yields. It does not set the bundle ID itself (not "bundle 0"): ambient thinkers get it from their spawn parameter, and the 2 sites are ambient_palette_cycler and PaletteResetAndKillThinker (actor_pool).
PaletteStart: COP #37 with one byte operand (palette bundle ID, 84 sites). Stores the ID in animScratch+2, zeroes the sub-entry index ($0E), loads sub-entry 0 with LoadPaletteBundle and applies it with DecompressGfxToVram. Then stores the address after the operand in $00 (the actor entry point) and yields with PLA, PLA, RTL, so the next frame resumes at the following op (normally PaletteStep).
PaletteStartLoop: COP #38 with two byte operands (bundle ID, pass count). Stores the ID in animScratch+2 and the pass count in retPtr1, zeroes the sub-entry index, applies sub-entry 0 and yields exactly like PaletteStart. The count is the TOTAL number of passes PaletteStepLoop makes through the bundle (a count of 0 would give 65,536 passes, by the DEC in StepLoop). Only 3 sites use it: two attack_ability_system effects (#2A/#4B with 2 passes) and one unused script.
PaletteStep: COP #39 with no operands (85 sites). Decrements the hold counter in spritesetPtr once per call. While it is still nonzero the counter is stored back, the current data pointer (animScratch) is copied to $08 and DecompressGfxToVram runs again, then the actor yields (the entry point saved by PaletteStart makes the same Step op run next frame). When the counter reaches zero LoadPaletteBundle loads the next sub-entry: carry clear = another frame, which is applied and the actor yields; carry set = end of bundle, so the script continues past this op with RTI and the sub-entry index has been reset to 0.
PaletteStepLoop: COP #3A with no operands. Same hold/frame logic as PaletteStep, but when LoadPaletteBundle reports the end of the bundle it decrements the pass counter in retPtr1: if nonzero it is stored and the bundle restarts at once (LoadPaletteBundle already reset the sub-entry index), and only when the counter reaches zero does the script continue with RTI. Pairs with PaletteStartLoop, which sets retPtr1.
ParseMapEntry:
Decodes a 3-byte stream record at address X into tile coordinates and metatile ID.

Zeroes direct page, reads 3 bytes from the stream: byte 0 = tile X, byte 1 = tile Y, byte 2 = metatile ID. If byte 0 has bit 7 set, returns carry set (end-of-stream sentinel). Otherwise sign-extends tile coords, computes pixel positions (×16) in DP $1A/$1E, stores tile coords in DP $18/$1C and metatile ID in DP $00, and returns carry clear. Called by WorldMapStream3/4 for sequential tile painting.
ParseSignedTileOffset: Internal JSR helper that reads two signed byte operands from the script pointer at $0A (D = actor slot). Sign-extends each offset, scales by 16 pixels, adds them to the actor position ($14/$16, with Y reduced by $10, one tile row), and converts the result to tile coordinates in $0018/$001C. Returns via RTS with $0A advanced past both operands. Called only by MarkSolidOffset and ClearSolidOffset; BranchIfSolidOffset repeats the arithmetic inline in pixel units.
PlaySoundBoth: COP #08 with one word operand (two SFX bytes packed). Stores the entire 16-bit value to sfxQueueCh1 as a word, filling both $06F8 and $06F9 in one write.
PlaySoundCh1: COP #07 with one byte operand (SFX ID). Writes the byte directly to sfxQueueCh1 ($06F8) for channel-1 sound effect playback.
PlaySoundCh2: COP #06 with one byte operand (SFX ID). Writes the byte directly to sfxQueueCh2 ($06F9) for channel-2 sound effect playback.
PrintDialogString: COP #BF with one word operand (text pointer). Sets dialogue mode ($2000), calls UpdateFrameRender, hides the status bar ($0800), renders via DialogStringRenderer, then clears directional joypad state in joypadCurrent and joypadHeld.
PrintDialogStringAlt: COP #6B with one word operand (text pointer). Like PrintDialogString but omits dialogue-mode setup and UpdateFrameRender; still hides the status bar, renders text, and clears joypadHeld directions.
ProcessAnimFlag: Internal JSR helper shared by all StageSpr variants. Clears frame counter $2A, then interprets the animation index byte: $FF leaves $28 unchanged (no-op), bit $80 set masks to the low 7 bits and conditionally sets horizontal flip ($4000 on $0E) based on actor flag $0002, and all other values store directly to $28 while clearing the flip bit. Returns via RTS.
QueueDma: COP #02 (28 sites). Same operands as QueueHdma (3-byte table address, B-bus register byte; used for window position registers #26, mode 7 matrix registers #1B–#1E, scroll registers and others). It calls SetupHdmaChannel_Direct, which writes DMAP WITHOUT the $40 flag and still sets the channel's bit in the HDMA enable mask, so this is a DIRECT-table HDMA channel (each table entry holds the register data inline), not a general linear DMA transfer. The name QueueDma is misleading; QueueHdma is the indirect variant.
QueueHdma: COP #01 (18 sites). Operands: a 3-byte table address (word + bank, e.g. $7E8800 or @label) and a byte naming the PPU B-bus register ($21xx, e.g. #0F = BG2HOFS). The handler reads them as two words: Y = address, A = bank (low byte) | register (high byte). SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect then picks the DMAP transfer mode from hdma_channel_config[register], ORs $40 (indirect addressing), uses the bank for both the table and the indirect data, and binds the NEXT free channel (allocated from channel 1 upward via $68/$6A; reset by ResetHdmaState). The channel is armed through the HDMA enable mask ($66).
QueueHdmaChannel: COP #03 (2 sites, both in scene_lifecycle: channels 6 and 7 for the BG1/BG2 horizontal scroll window). Operands: a byte channel number (0–7), a 3-byte table address, and a byte B-bus register. Unlike #01/#02 it programs the named channel directly: register block offset = channel × 16 ($4300 + offset), channel bit ORed into the HDMA enable mask $66, DMAP = hdma_channel_config[register] | $40 (indirect), DASB = A1B = bank, BBAD = register, A1T = table address. The handler PHYs the slot and PLXes it back at the end instead of using TYX, and uses WRAM $0000/$0002 as scratch.
QueueMapChange: COP #26 with one byte (scene ID), two words (X, Y position), one byte (flags), and one word (extra data). Writes map-transition staging data to $0642–$0652; if flags bit 7 is set, also saves the script PC and bank to sceneSaveData for post-transition restoration.
ReadDirSprite_YVelocity:
Advances the forced-walk data stream and resolves south/north sprite frame plus Y-axis animation duration.

Increments the stream pointer at $0650, reads the next direction byte, looks up a base sprite frame in direction_velocity_table (stored to $0000), and fetches a movement-delta index into movement_delta_table (stored to $2E as frame duration). Has a sibling ReadDirSprite_XVelocity for east/west walks.
ReadDivideResult: Hardware divide latency wrapper. Five NOPs provide the 16-cycle wait required after writing WRDIVB before the SNES hardware divider result is valid, then reads RDDIVL into A. Called by MultiplyThenDivide.
ReadMultiplyResult: Hardware multiply latency wrapper. One NOP provides the 8-cycle wait required after writing WRMPYB before the SNES hardware multiplier result is valid, then reads RDMPYL into Y. Called by MultiplyThenDivide.
ReloadMoveDurations: COP #B1 with no operands. Re-runs AnimFrameLookup for the current moveXAlt and moveYAlt values, refreshing frame durations at actor+$2C and +$2E.
RemoveItem: COP #D5 with one byte operand (item ID). Calls RemoveItemFromInventory (zeroes the matching slot and, as a side effect, resets the equipped state: inventoryEquippedType = 0, inventoryEquippedIndex = $FFFF) and continues.
ResetSpriteState: COP #55 (script name ResetSpriteInit) sprite/animation reset taking one byte and one word operand. Stores the animation index in $28, clears the frame counter $2A, and sets the spriteset/script bank pointer $24. Does not advance animation itself — it reinitializes state before StageSpr/AnimOnce sequences.
ResetVector: CPU reset entry point. Disables interrupts, clears carry, switches from 65816 emulation mode to native mode via XCE, then jumps long to SystemInit.
ResolveActorIndex: Internal JSR helper that converts an 8-bit actor list index in A to a WRAM actor pointer in Y. Computes Y = index × $30 + $1000 using SignedMultiply, matching the fixed $30-byte actor structure layout. Called by BranchIfActorNear and BranchIfActorAt before distance or coordinate comparisons.
ResolveTileData:
Converts parsed tile coordinates to a map-layer index and writes metatile and collision data.

Calls TileCoordsToMapIndex (DP $18/$1C → linear index in X), reads the collision byte from animScratch[index], writes the metatile ID to mapLayerTilemap[index] and collision byte to collisionLayer[index]. Then checks if the tile is on-screen by comparing pixel X against BG1 scroll and pixel Y against BG2 scroll. When visible, expands the metatile into four 16×16 VRAM tile words from metatileMapLayer, stages them in the tile-update queue ($0904–$090C), and computes the VRAM address pair via PixelToVramAddress. Called by DrawMetatileAbs/Here and WorldMapStream3/4.
RestorePlayerControl:
Restores normal player locomotion after a climb or ramp animation finishes.

Resets the player actor entry pointer to PlayerIdleEntry, clears velocity scratch at $002C/$002E/$0008, adjusts status word $0010 (clears $0200, sets $0008), unmasks joypad ($0F00), and clears playerFlags $0800. Called from UnlockPlayerAfterClimb and from ramp exit handlers in ramps.asm.
RestoreSavedPtr: COP #C5 with no operands. If retPtr1 ($7F0004) is non-zero, restores it as the script PC and clears retPtr1; otherwise yields via RTL.
ResumeAfterSnap: COP #4A with no operands. Restores the saved script PC and bank from snapResumePtr ($7F1018) and $7F101A after grid snapping completes, then clears both save slots.
ReturnWithSignal: COP #E1 with no operands. Restores the deferred call PC from retPtr1 (clearing it); if set, RTI-resumes with A=$FFFF as a non-zero signal to the caller, otherwise yields via RTL.
RngByte: COP #23 with no operands. Advances a 16-byte Galois LFSR chain at $040F–$041F and returns the latest output byte from $0410 in A.
RngMod: COP #24 with one byte operand (modulus). Applies repeated subtraction modulo to the current RngByte output ($0410) and stores the result in rngModuloResult ($0420).
RunBg3Script: COP #BD BG3 console-script runner taking one Address operand: a far pointer to a BG3 tilemap command stream. Switches data bank, calls ConsoleStringRenderer with direct page zeroed, then sets displayModeFlags bit 0 to mark HUD/console rendering active. Used by the diary menu, title screen, and boot-logo actors for text and menu drawing.
RunPlayerAnim: COP #93 with no operands. Calls UpdateActorAnimation once per script tick; clears $2C/$2E when the animation finishes (carry set). Yields via RTL while the animation is still running.
ScrollCameraAccumulate:
Accumulative camera scroll actor-def used in Pyramid interior scenes.

Initializes X/Y accumulator registers at DP $24 and $26 to zero, tile-aligns position, then each frame calls ComputeScrollDeltas and adds the accumulators to cameraDeltaX and cameraDeltaY. External actors can pre-load $24/$26 to inject extra drift on top of standard tracking.
ScrollCameraInit:
Camera initialization scroll actor.

Sets bit 12 ($1000) in actor status as a camera-active flag. Subtracts centering offsets (−8px X, −16px Y) from position parameters and aligns both axes to the 16×16 tile grid via TileAlignCoord.

Runs a 3-iteration ramp-up loop (COP LoopInit with count 3) that computes scroll deltas each iteration via ComputeScrollDeltas. After the loop, saves the final Y delta to savedCameraDelta ($0690).

Then sets the actor entry point (COP SetEntryHere) for per-frame execution, computes deltas one more time, and forces the X scroll by writing cameraDeltaX with bit 15 set to forcedScrollOverride ($06C8). The normal cameraDeltaX is zeroed since the forced override takes precedence.

Used during scene transitions where the camera needs to snap to a position, ramp up smoothly, then maintain a forced horizontal scroll.
ScrollCameraTrack:
Simple continuous camera tracking actor.

Sets the camera-active flag, aligns position parameters to the tile grid via TileAlignPosition, then enters a per-frame loop (COP SetEntryHere). Each frame, both X and Y scroll deltas are recomputed by ComputeScrollDeltas using the current camera targets and speed parameters.

The simplest scroll mode — used when the camera should smoothly follow the player with no special behavior.
ScrollCameraVertical:
Vertical-only camera tracking actor-def referenced from scene_actors in Edward's Castle, Itory, Incan Ruins, and Dao.

Sets camera-active flag $1000, tile-aligns position via TileAlignPosition, then loops with SetEntryHere computing only the Y scroll delta through MulDivide when speed parameter $16 is nonzero. Leaves cameraDeltaX unchanged from any prior scroll actor. X speed parameter $14 is ignored entirely.
SetCollideCallback: COP #5A with one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in onCollideCallback ($7F1008) for collision-event dispatch.
SetCollisionAbs: COP #42 (legacy name SetSolidAbs) absolute collision writer taking three byte operands: tile X, tile Y, and a full collision-layer byte value. Converts the tile coordinates through TileCoordsToMapIndex and stores the byte directly into collisionLayer, replacing both nibbles (solid and type) in one write. Used once in the game. The handler has no TYX: it pushes Y (the slot) at entry and recovers it with PLX at the end, after X has been used for the map index.
SetCustomCallback: COP #5E with one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in the custom-callback word ($7F1016, written as scratch1010+6) of the actor's slot. combat_collision runs it as the interaction handler for push hits; some actors reuse the word for other data.
SetDeathCallback: COP #57 with an @Code far-pointer operand (word + bank byte, 3 bytes). Stores the word in onDeathCallback ($7F1004) and the bank in the following word ($7F1006), both indexed by actor slot, for the death script hook.
SetDodgeCallback: COP #59 with one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in onDodgeCallback ($7F1002) for dodge-event dispatch.
SetDungeonKillFlag: COP #D8 with no script operands. Reads the actor's enemyNum ($7F:0022,X — the dungeon enemy number used for kill tracking) as a flag index and, when its low byte is non-zero, calls SetWramFlag to set that bit in the scene-local wramFlags bitfield ($0A80, cleared at scene boundaries), recording the kill. Index 0 is ignored.
SetEntryFar: COP #E2 with one Address operand (word+bank). Writes the far entry pointer to $00/$02, zeroes $08, and RTI-continues immediately without yielding.
SetEntryHere: COP #C1 with no operands. Saves the current script bank ($0C→$02) and PC ($0A→$00) as the actor entry/resume pointer without yielding.
SetEntryHereAndYield: COP #C2 with no operands. Same entry-pointer save as SetEntryHere, then pops the return address and yields via RTL so execution resumes next frame.
SetEventFlag: Core JSR routine that sets one bit in the eventFlags ($0A00) bitfield. Decomposes the flag index into byte (÷8) and bit (AND $07) indices, ORs the bitmasks_bit_position entry into the eventFlags byte. Called by all SetFlag COP handlers and JSL offset wrappers.
SetEventFlag_0200: JSL helper (not COP-dispatched) that sets a persistent event flag in the $0200+ eventFlags array. Expects the flag index in A, adds base $0200, and calls SetEventFlag to OR the corresponding bit. Called from warps_interaction chest handling and hidden_red_jewel to permanently mark one-shot world events.
SetFlag_0100: JSL helper that sets an event flag at base $0100 (boss/dungeon defeat flags). Masks to byte, adds $0100, and calls SetEventFlag.
SetFlag_0300: JSL helper that sets an event flag at base $0300 (scene-scoped flags). Masks to byte, adds $0300, and calls SetEventFlag.
SetFlagByte: COP #CC with one byte operand (flag index). Calls SetEventFlag to OR the corresponding bit in the eventFlags ($0A00) bitfield.
SetFlagRaw: JSL helper that sets an event flag without adding a base offset. Masks to byte and calls SetEventFlag directly.
SetFlagWord: COP #CD with one word operand (flag index). Calls SetEventFlag with the 16-bit flag number.
SetHitCallback: COP #58 with one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in onHitCallback ($7F1000) for hit-event dispatch.
SetHMirror: COP #BB with no operands. Sets horizontal mirror bit $4000 on OAM attribute word $0E via TSB.
SetInteractHandler: COP #C0 (script name SetOnInteract) NPC interaction handler setter taking one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in the actor chatPtr field ($7F000A), which the interaction system invokes when the player talks to or touches the actor. Used by virtually all NPCs, chests, and inspectable objects.
SetLinkedEntryPtr:
COP $6A (SetLinkedEntryPtr) with one &Code operand: point the next-linked actor ($06) at a new script.

Only the 16-bit word at the linked actor's $00/$01 is replaced (the 2-byte operand is a same-bank pointer; its bank byte $02 is left as it was), and its waitCounter ($08) and moveX/moveY ($2C/$2E) are zeroed so the new script starts on the linked actor's next tick with no pending wait or velocity. The caller's script pointer is advanced past the operand and the COP returns via RTI, so the caller continues immediately.

Y = linked actor's DP base; $0000,Y works as that actor's DP because DBR=$81 mirrors low WRAM.
SetMetasprite: COP #88 with one word plus one byte operand. Sets spritesetPtr ($7F0006) and spriteset bank ($7F0008) to point the actor at a new metasprite table.
SetOamPalette: COP #B7 with one byte operand (0–7). Clears palette bits $0E00 in $0E, then XBA/TSB to set the 4-bit OAM palette subfield.
SetOamPriority: COP #B6 with one byte operand (0–3). Clears OAM priority bits $3000 in attribute word $0E, then XBA/TSB to pack the value into the high byte.
SetPlayerSpriteDirect: COP #8E with one byte operand (body index). Multiplies the index by six to index 6-byte body_table entries, writes spritesetPtr and bank byte ($7F0008), caches the index in animScratch2, and sets playerFlags bit $8000.
SetPriorityMax: COP #B2 with no operands. Sets bit $0002 on actor+$10 via TSB: SortActorsByDepth then gives the actor key $0000 (first OAM index), so it draws in front of every other actor.
SetPriorityMin: COP #B3 with no operands. Sets bit $0001 on actor+$10 via TSB: SortActorsByDepth then gives the actor key $01FE (last OAM index), so it draws behind every other actor unless SetPriorityMax is also set.
SetSavedPtr: COP #C6 with one &Code operand. Stores the operand offset as a deferred-return pointer in retPtr1 ($7F0004) for later RestoreSavedPtr/ReturnWithSignal use.
SetScratchPointer: COP #54 with one word plus one byte operand. Stores the far pointer in animScratch ($7F0000 word, $7F0002 bank) for later use by handler or callback code.
SetTilePos: COP #25 with two byte operands (tile X, tile Y). Converts tile coordinates to pixel positions by shifting each ×16; adds 8 to X for horizontal tile-centering and stores results in actor $14/$16.
SetWramFlag: Core JSR routine that sets one bit in the wramFlags ($0A80) bitfield. Decomposes the flag index: byte = index÷8 (LSR×3), bit = index AND $07, then ORs the corresponding bitmasks_bit_position entry into the wramFlags byte. Called by SetDungeonKillFlag and all SetWramFlag JSL wrappers.
SetWramFlag_Offset100: JSL helper that sets a WRAM flag at base $0100. Masks the index to 3 bits, adds $0100, and calls SetWramFlag. Pairs with TestWramFlag_Offset100 for boss/dungeon defeat flags.
smooth_follow_child: Entry point: spawn a SmoothFollowChildTick child for per-frame position updates, pass target ref ($24), then idle-animate until parent sets $4000 kill flag.
SmoothFollowApplyEastPrimary: Apply follow step when target is east and |deltaY| dominates: Y += step, X += step.
SmoothFollowApplyEastSecondary: Apply follow step when target is east-secondary (SW quadrant): Y += step, X -= step.
SmoothFollowApplySouthPrimary: Apply follow step when target is south-primary (NW when |deltaY| dominates): Y -= step, X -= step.
SmoothFollowApplyWestPrimary: Apply follow step when target is west and |deltaX| dominates: X -= step, Y += step.
SmoothFollowApplyWestSecondary: Apply follow step when target is west-secondary (NW quadrant): X -= step, Y -= step.
SmoothFollowChildDie: Kill entry point, also used as default collision callback by combat_collision for non-combat actors.
SmoothFollowChildTick: Per-frame tick: compute relative offset (target - self) for X and Y, determine which quadrant the target is in, then dispatch to the appropriate directional follow routine. Y offset is biased by -8px to center on the sprite midpoint.
SmoothFollowWriteParentPos: Write this actor's updated position back to the parent actor's position fields.
SnapToGrid: COP #43 with no operands. If the actor is not 16×16 tile-aligned ((X−8)|Y & $0F ≠ 0), saves snapResumePtr/$7F101A and yields RTI into EnemyPositionSnap; otherwise continues immediately.
SpawnAfter: COP #9B with one Address operand. Calls AllocateActorAfter (list insert + CopyActorState), then sets the new actor script entry pointer from the operand.
SpawnAfterAbs: COP #9F with one Address plus two word operands (absolute X/Y). Spawns after the current actor and assigns $0014/$0016 directly from the operand words.
SpawnAfterAbsFlags: COP #A0 with one Address, two words (X/Y), and one word (flags). SpawnAfterAbs with status flags written to $0010.
SpawnAfterAbsMarked: COP #A3 with one Address, two words (X/Y), and one word (flags). SpawnAfterAbsFlags plus $0040 flag and MarkChildActor.
SpawnAfterFlags: COP #9C with one Address plus one word operand. SpawnAfter plus an initial status-flags word written to $0010.
SpawnAfterMarked: COP #A2 with one Address plus one word (flags). SpawnAfterFlags variant that sets spawner flag $0040 and calls MarkChildActor for parent–child lifecycle tracking.
SpawnAfterOffset: COP #9D with one Address plus two word operands (X/Y offset). Spawns after the current actor and adds the 16-bit offset words to the new actor $0014/$0016.
SpawnAfterOffsetFlags: COP #9E with one Address, two word offsets, and one word (flags). SpawnAfterOffset with an additional status-flags word stored in $0010.
SpawnAfterOffsetMarked: COP #A4 with one Address, two signed bytes (X/Y offset), and one word (flags). Spawns after current actor with sign-extended byte offsets added to $0014/$0016, sets flags, ORs $0040, and calls MarkChildActor.
SpawnBefore: COP #99 with one Address operand (word+bank entry pointer). Calls AllocateActorBefore (which inserts a list slot and CopyActorState from the spawner), then writes the script entry address to the new actor $0000/$0002.
SpawnBeforeFlags: COP #9A with one Address plus one word operand. Same as SpawnBefore, additionally writing the word operand to the spawned actor status flags ($0010).
SpawnBeforeMarked: COP #A1 with one Address plus one word (flags). SpawnBeforeFlags variant that also ORs $0040 into the spawner flags ($12) and calls MarkChildActor to link parent and child.
SpawnListAppend: COP #A5 with one Address, two signed bytes (X/Y offset), and one word (flags). Uses ActorPoolAllocator and appends the new slot at the actor-list tail ($0058), CopyActorState, then applies entry pointer, signed offsets, and flags. On pool exhaustion (carry set) skips all operands without spawning.
SpawnListAppendSpr: COP #A6 with one Address, one byte (animation index), two signed bytes (X/Y offset), and one word (flags). Like SpawnListAppend but also stores an animation index byte in the spawned actor $0028; skips one extra operand byte on pool exhaustion.
SpawnThinker: COP #3C with one Address operand. Same as SpawnThinkerParam but skips the param byte; allocates a special thinker actor and sets its entry pointer from the script operand.
SpawnThinkerParam: COP #3B with one byte (init param) plus one Address (entry pointer). Allocates a special actor via AllocateSpecialActor, stores param in animScratch+2, writes the far entry pointer to $0000/$0002, copies caller animScratch2, and clears $000E.
speed_zone_ew_fast:
Invisible east–west fast-movement zone actor used in Kress Maze and Mountain Temple.

Uses the same 16×16 proximity test as speed_zone_ew_slow but writes $0007 (+7) to playerSpeedEw when the player is inside the zone. Paired with speed_zone_ew_slow and speed_zone_ns_slow to create directional current lanes.
speed_zone_ew_slow:
Invisible east–west slow-movement zone actor placed in Mountain Temple and related scenes.

When the player center lies within a 16×16 pixel box around the actor, writes $FFF9 (−7) to global playerSpeedEw ($09B4). Returns immediately if the player is outside the zone.
speed_zone_ns_slow:
Invisible north–south slow-movement zone actor with a tighter vertical window than the east–west variants.

Requires the player to be within 16 pixels horizontally and within 4 pixels vertically of the actor center, then sets playerSpeedNs to $FFF9 (−7). Placed in Mountain Temple scenes alongside the EW zones.
SpiralStep: COP #6D with two signed byte operands (diameter delta, angle delta). Adds them to orbitDiameter and orbitAngle, then calls ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef using the actor reference in $0000 to reposition orbitally.
StageBgChange: COP #32 with one byte operand: an event-block index. Calls event_blocks.LookupEventBlock, which matches the entry against sceneCurrent and loads its source/destination tile rectangles into the event-block work variables; nothing is drawn yet (the paired ApplyBgChange animates it). LookupEventBlock's carry result (set = no entry for this scene) is ignored.
StageBgChangeFromDeathIdx: COP #34 with no operands. Uses the actor's deathActionIdx ($7F0024, the event-block byte of its scene record) as the event-block index, queues SFX $0F on both sound channels, then jumps into StageBgChange's LookupEventBlock tail to stage the swap. Only SpawnFieldRevealEffect uses it.
StageMove: COP #52 with three byte operands (animation index, speed, frame delay). Computes signed pixel deltas from moveXAlt/moveYAlt vs current position, repeatedly halves them while the high byte is non-zero, divides total distance by signed speed for frame count, and initializes TickMove state before RTI continuation.
StageMoveX: COP #AA with one byte operand (movement index). Stores it in moveXAlt and sets animation frame duration at actor+$2C via AnimFrameLookup.
StageMoveXY: COP #AC with two byte operands (X index, Y index). Stages both moveXAlt/moveYAlt and refreshes frame durations at $2C and $2E via AnimFrameLookup.
StageMoveY: COP #AB with one byte operand (movement index). Stores it in moveYAlt and sets animation frame duration at actor+$2E via AnimFrameLookup.
StagePlayerSpr: COP #8F with one byte operand (animation index). Stores the anim in actor $28, clears $2A, calls SetActorBody to apply the current characterForm body, then saves the script PC/bank in $00/$02 for deferred animation staging.
StagePlayerSprFromDP: COP #95 with no script operands. Reads the animation index from direct-page $0000 instead of the script stream, then runs SetActorBody and saves $00/$02 like StagePlayerSpr.
StagePlayerSprWall: COP #94 with four byte operands (animation index, X distance, Y distance, wall type). Identical XY staging to StagePlayerSprXY, plus a fourth byte stored in playerWallType ($09B0) for subsequent wall-collision checks.
StagePlayerSprX: COP #90 with two byte operands (animation index, X step). Same SetActorBody staging as StagePlayerSpr, stores X distance in moveXAlt ($7F0018), and uses AnimFrameLookup to resolve the X frame duration into $2C.
StagePlayerSprXY: COP #92 with three byte operands (animation index, X distance, Y distance). Combines both axis staging: SetActorBody, then AnimFrameLookup for X→$2C and Y→$2E, with moveXAlt/moveYAlt updated.
StagePlayerSprY: COP #91 with two byte operands (animation index, Y step). Like StagePlayerSprX but stores Y distance in moveYAlt ($7F001A) and writes the looked-up Y frame duration to $2E.
StageSpr: COP #80 with one byte operand (animation index). Calls ProcessAnimFlag to set $28 (with optional horizontal flip on $0E) and refreshes script bank/pointer fields from $0C/$0A.
StageSprAndHitbox: COP #8D with one byte operand (animation index). Runs ProcessAnimFlag, immediately calls UpdateActorAnimation to refresh sprite and hitbox data, resets $2A to zero, and updates script bank/pointer fields.
StageSprLoop: COP #84 with two byte operands (animation index, loop count). Runs ProcessAnimFlag and stores the loop count in sprTimer for use by AnimLoop.
StageSprLoopX: COP #85 with three byte operands (animation index, loop count, X distance). Runs ProcessAnimFlag, sets sprTimer, stores moveXAlt, and computes $2C via AnimFrameLookup.
StageSprLoopXY: COP #87 with four byte operands (animation index, loop count, X distance, Y distance). Runs ProcessAnimFlag, sets sprTimer, and computes both $2C and $2E via AnimFrameLookup.
StageSprLoopY: COP #86 with three byte operands (animation index, loop count, Y distance). Runs ProcessAnimFlag, sets sprTimer, stores moveYAlt, and computes $2E via AnimFrameLookup.
StageSprX: COP #81 with two byte operands (animation index, X distance). Runs ProcessAnimFlag, stores X distance in moveXAlt, and sets frame duration $2C via AnimFrameLookup.
StageSprXY: COP #83 with three byte operands (animation index, X distance, Y distance). Runs ProcessAnimFlag and AnimFrameLookup for both axes, setting $2C and $2E.
StageSprY: COP #82 with two byte operands (animation index, Y distance). Runs ProcessAnimFlag, stores Y distance in moveYAlt, and sets frame duration $2E via AnimFrameLookup.
StageWorldMapChoice: COP #66 with two word operands (start X, Y in pixels) plus one byte (selection ID, 1–$1B in overworld_exit). Writes worldMapStagedX ($0D52), worldMapPlayerY ($0D56) and worldMapChoiceId ($0D58); WorldMapController dispatches a nonzero choice ID through world_map_options. Does not warp immediately.
StageWorldMapMove: COP #65 with two word and two byte operands: world-map start X, start Y (pixels), a byte stored to $0D5E (0 in every shipped script; no reader found), and a route ID stored to worldMapRouteId ($0D5A, index into world_map_routes). Clears worldMapChoiceId so the route plays directly instead of opening a selection. Does not warp immediately. Used by NPC scripts in Dao, Itory, Watermia, Freejia, Edward Castle, Euro, Nazca, Native Village, South Cape and Angel Village.
StageWorldMapMoveIds: COP #67 with two byte operands: a byte stored to $0D5E (always 0 in shipped scripts; no reader found) and a route ID stored to worldMapRouteId ($0D5A). Used by the world_map_options handlers after the player picks a destination.
StairTriggerSouth:
South-facing stair trigger actor-def placed on stair tiles in scene_actors (e.g. Mu Passage and other dungeons).

Each frame it checks whether the player is within an 8–32 pixel Y band aligned to the trigger row, shares the trigger X column, is in a walking move state ($8F via CheckMoveState), and faces south (sprite index $0012 or $0013). On success it redirects the player entry pointer to ClimbSouth and calls LockPlayerForClimb.
StandardEnemyDefeatHandler:
Main entry for the standard field-enemy death pipeline; reached when an enemy's HP hits zero.

Expects X = defeated actor index; reads statsPtr and extendedFlags to distinguish normal enemies, stat-table entries, and boss-flag ($0080) actors. Non-boss kills decrement BCD counters $0AEE/$0AEC and stash the remaining count in orbitAngle before falling into the shared defeat sequence. The sequence plays death SFX, spawns EnemyDeathFlash, routes gem drops or stat rewards, and ends with COP Die.
StartMusic: COP #04 music-start handler taking one byte operand: the music bundle ID. Allocates a new actor slot via AllocateActorAfter, sets its entry point to SpcTransferMusicData, sets status bit $1000 and clears $0800, and stores the music ID in chatPtr. The spawned transfer actor handles the SPC handshake asynchronously. Used in cutscenes throughout the game.
SwitchCase: COP #D9 with two word operands: a low-WRAM address holding the switch variable, and the base (in the script bank) of a table of word script addresses. Reads the byte at the WRAM address, doubles it, fetches the word at base + 2×value (DBR temporarily set to the script bank cached in $0C) and makes it the new script address. There is no range check — a value past the end of the table reads whatever follows it. The doubled index is kept in scratch word $0000, so a script that uses $0000 itself as the variable has it overwritten.
SystemInit:
Full system boot sequence and main game loop.

Boot phase:
1. Sets native 65816 mode with 16-bit registers
2. Initializes direct page ($0000), stack ($01FF), data bank ($81)
3. Enables FastROM access speed
4. Calls hardware register init, system variable init, SPC engine load
5. Enables display and sets world-ready flag
6. Checks warmboot signature at $000100 for scene selection
7. Initializes gameplay defaults: movement speeds, defense, HP, slope curves, ability slots
8. Sets starting scene to $FB (title screen)

Main loop (infinite):
1. VBlank wait and joypad read
2. Scene management and warp/chest checks
3. Actor AI processing and sprite composition
4. Camera scrolling for both BG layers
5. HUD update and display list flush
6. Enable NMI and loop
TestEventFlag: Core JSR routine that tests one bit in the eventFlags ($0A00) bitfield. ANDs the bitmasks_bit_position entry against the eventFlags byte, then uses SEC/BNE/CLC to return carry set if the bit is set, carry clear if clear. Called by BranchOnFlag, WaitOnFlag COP handlers and all TestFlag JSL wrappers.
TestEventFlag_0200: JSL helper that tests an event flag at base $0200 (persistent world events). Masks to byte, adds $0200, and calls TestEventFlag. Returns carry set if set.
TestFlag_0100: JSL helper that tests an event flag at base $0100. Masks to byte, adds $0100, and calls TestEventFlag.
TestFlag_0300: JSL helper that tests an event flag at base $0300 (scene-scoped flags). Masks to byte, adds $0300, and calls TestEventFlag.
TestFlag_0510: JSL helper that tests an event flag at base $0510 (late-game progression). Masks to byte, adds $0510, and calls TestEventFlag.
TestFlagRaw: JSL helper that tests an event flag without adding a base offset. Masks to byte and calls TestEventFlag directly.
TestWramFlag: Core JSR routine that tests one bit in the wramFlags ($0A80) bitfield. Uses the same byte/bit decomposition as SetWramFlag, ANDs the bit mask against the wramFlags byte, and returns carry set if the flag is set, carry clear otherwise.
TestWramFlag_Offset100: JSL helper (not COP-dispatched) that tests a WRAM flag in the $0100–$0107 bit-flag range. Expects the flag index (0–7) in A, masks to three bits, adds base $0100, and calls TestWramFlag; returns carry set if the flag is set, carry clear otherwise. Used by boss and dungeon scripts to check defeat/reward flags.
TickGravity: COP #64 with no operands. Increments a tick counter and applies quadratic acceleration (tick² × factor) via hardware multiply to update velocity; RTI returns A=$FFFF when the actor reaches moveYAlt target, otherwise A=$0000.
TickMove: COP #53 with no operands. Per-frame companion to StageMove: MovementVelocityCompute uses hardware multiply/divide to advance position on both axes, waits on UpdateActorAnimation when needed, and yields RTL until the staged trajectory (and any halving passes) completes.
TickMoveComplete: End-of-pass handler for TickMove. Checks chatPtr for remaining halving passes: if non-zero, decrements it, zeroes animScratch and tick counter $24, and jumps back to TickMoveStep for another interpolation pass at halved scale. When chatPtr reaches zero, saves the script PC to $00 and yields RTL to resume the calling script.
TickSineHdma: COP #60 with one byte (delay) and one byte (camera-reference index). Decrements/reloads the delay counter in animScratch+2, advances retPtr1, selects camera X/Y from cameraTarget arrays, and rebuilds the sine HDMA table via BuildSineHdmaTable.
TileAlignCoord:
Converts a pixel coordinate to a tile-grid-aligned value.

Switches to 8-bit accumulator, shifts right 4 times (divides by 16 — the metatile width), then restores 16-bit mode and masks with $0F0F to isolate valid 4-bit tile indices in both the high and low bytes. The result is transferred to Y for the caller to store.

The 8-bit shift is key: by operating in 8-bit mode, the LSR operations independently divide the high and low bytes of the 16-bit value, producing two separate 4-bit tile indices packed into a word.
TileAlignPosition:
Applies tile-grid alignment to both camera position parameters.

Subtracts 8 pixels from the X position ($14) to center the camera horizontally on the player sprite midpoint before aligning. The Y position ($16) is aligned without any centering offset.

Both axes are processed through TileAlignCoord, and the aligned results (in Y register) are stored back to their respective DP locations.
TileCollisionQuery: Internal JSR helper that probes one tile of the $7FC000 collision layer. The probe pixel (WRAM $0018 = X, $001C = Y) must lie inside the camera bounds rectangle (cameraOffsetX/Y up to cameraBoundsX/cameraLowerYBound, X masked to a 16-pixel boundary); it is converted to tile coordinates (Y reduced by one more row), mapped with CalcTileMapOffset, and the collision byte is read through [$80],Y.
